title: First-commit SDK telemetry & contracts playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the "first-commit" surface of any Redwood SDK (JS/Python/Go). Focus: minimal onboarding experience + a small, explicit telemetry and API contract that protects product metrics and lets infra teams safely evolve implementations without surprises.

Audience:
- SDK engineers shipping initial GA SDKs
- Developer-experience writers and examples owners
- Serving/runtime and infra teams that rely on telemetry

Problem statement (short):
New SDKs frequently ship with inconsistent event names, ambiguous error codes, and missing version telemetry. That causes noisy pipeline work (alert thrash), hard-to-reproduce customer issues, and downstream metric gaps. This doc sketches a minimal, enforceable contract to include at the time of first public commit and quickstart.

Non-goals:
- Full telemetry schema for every feature (defer to DE-telemetry canonical spec).
- Heavy-weight privacy or legal wording (ops will add KMS/Pii rules in private-deployments docs).

High-level requirements for first commit: (MUST have)
- SDK exposes a single top-level client factory and one quickstart snippet (sub-10 lines) that works with a free API key.
- Telemetry events: sdk.init, request.start, request.end, request.error, sdk.version. Each event must include 'sdk_name', 'sdk_version', 'client_id' (UUID), 'region', and 'model' when applicable.
- Errors follow the lightweight contract: error.code (string), error.class (client|server|usage|network), error.message (human), request_id (server-propagated if available).
- Quickstart README includes a "What to do if things fail" troubleshooting section mapping error.class -> next steps.

Telemetry event shape (minimal):
- sdk.init: { sdk_name, sdk_version, client_id, time, env (dev|prod|test) }
- request.start: { sdk_name, sdk_version, client_id, request_id_local, model, prompt_length, intent_tag? }
- request.end: { request_id_local, server_request_id?, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, success: true }
- request.error: { request_id_local, error.code, error.class, error.message, stack? }
- sdk.version: emitted at startup and on upgrade migrations (only if version changes at runtime e.g., hot-reload)

Implementation guidance (practical):
- Keep the telemetry client optional behind a single flag (enableTelemetry: true|false) defaulting to true for hosted SDK samples but false in private-deploy quickstarts.
- Provide a deterministic client_id generator (v4 UUID) persisted to the OS keyring or ~/.redwood/sdk-meta.json; document privacy implications.
- Use non-blocking fire-and-forget HTTP to the telemetry collector with a 50ms soft timeout; failures must be swallowed and increment a local metric only.

Quickstart outline (for README and first-run):
1) One-liner install (npm/pip/go get).
2) 8-line snippet: init, call generate/chat, print response. Inline comment on how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY.
3) Troubleshooting section: how to read error.contract fields and where to find request_id in console.
4) Telemetry summary: what we collect and why; link to privacy page.
5) Local emulation note: how to run against a local dev server (env var REDWOOD_API_URL).

Docs checklist before first-public commit: (checkbox style for PR authors)
- [ ] Quickstart snippet runs in CI (unit test that executes sample with test key).
- [ ] Telemetry toggle present and documented.
- [ ] Error mapping table included in README matching runtime classes.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry template exists for breaking API changes.
- [ ] Example showing how to pin model versions and what fallback looks like.

Release / rollout plan for an initial SDK publish:
- Stage 0 (internal): merge behind feature flag, internal devs test quickstart and telemetry flows (1 week).
- Stage 1 (canary): release to NPM/PyPI with dist-tag 'canary' and announce to 10 internal partners (2 weeks). Collect metrics: quickstart success rate, first-run latency, request.error rate.
- Stage 2 (public): promote to 'latest' if canary metrics stable for 7 days. Create a 'migration guide' PR if any non-trivial behavior changed.

Key metrics to monitor (first-30d):
- first-run success rate (CI sample snippet pass / total attempts)
- quickstart-to-prod conversion: proportion of users who run quickstart then call production endpoints within 7d
- telemetry opt-out rate (if present)
- request.error rate and distribution by error.class
- avg latency p50/p95 for quickstart calls

Sample error mapping table (to include in README):
- client.invalid_api_key -> client -> "check env var / ask for correct key"
- client.rate_limited -> client -> "backoff with exponential jitter; see retry policy"
- server.overloaded -> server -> "retry after, fallback to smaller model or region"
- network.timeout -> network -> "check proxy, network connectivity"

Developer experience notes / TODOs (rough):
- Add a small unit test harness under examples/quickstart-test that runs the snippet against a local mock and asserts telemetry events were emitted.
- Pair with infra team to expose a small 'sample' telemetry stream in staging so SDK teams can validate event shapes quickly. (Ticket: DE-telemetry-bridge)
- Write a short internal explainer doc for support engineers: how to map request_id_local -> server_request_id for cross-service debug.
- Decide default telemetry retention for first-party SDKs (30 days?) and confirm with privacy.

Open questions (to resolve before GA):
- Should client_id be considered PII? (privacy wants a review; mark for legal review).
- What is the canonical name for intent_tag on request.start? (consistency across SDKs matters.)
- Do we include prompt snapshots in telemetry for debug? (default: NO – only include hashed prompt_id)

Appendix: quick example (JS pseudo):
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, enableTelemetry: true });
const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-3b', prompt: 'Summarize the following...' });
console.log(r.text);
// telemetry: sdk.init, request.start -> send async, request.end -> send async

Next steps (short):
- Get approval from infra/observability for event shapes (owners: Miguel Lopez).
- File legal/privacy review for client_id persistence (owner: Priya Desai).
- Create GH PR template that includes the docs checklist above (owner: Aisha).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lightweight and prescriptive. The goal is to remove repeated rework when new SDKs are created; enforce a small consistent surface that observability and support can depend on.

References and links:
- DE telemetry canonical (Confluence): /display/DE/Telemetry+Schema
- Example GH PR that implemented similar pattern in infra: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/289
- Jira: DE-987 (telemetry bridge), DE-1012 (quickstart CI test)
